title: Per-client embedding scoring mode and safe migration path for reranker correctness
creator: Priya Desai
description:
Summary:
Customers are observing inconsistent ranking behavior when switching between SDK versions and between embedding model variants. Root cause analysis shows two major axes: (1) whether stored embeddings are L2-normalized before indexing and (2) whether scoring consumers use cosine similarity or raw dot product (and whether any implicit scaling was applied during model export). Historically we shipped embeddings without explicit normalization metadata and relied on client libraries to normalize at query time, creating subtle backward-compatibility gaps when clients upgrade or when we change runtime batching/scale behavior.

Goals:
- Make scoring behavior explicit and reproducible across SDKs, runtime, and persisted index storage.
- Provide a safe, opt-in legacy compatibility mode that preserves historical scores for customers who depend on them.
- Add telemetry and unit tests to detect metric/drift regressions early.
- Keep a migration path that minimizes re-indexing cost for large datasets.

Proposed solution (high level):
1) Introduce per-client scoring_mode metadata stored in account metadata: one of ["dot","cosine","auto"]. Default = "auto".
2) Embed normative embedding metadata at time of creation: store l2_norm (float) and a boolean normalized_flag when embeddings are normalized server-side. This is optional for storage backends with space concerns; default behavior for new embeddings is to store l2_norm only.
3) Reranker adapter in the runtime will compute scores using an explicit transform chain: if scoring_mode=="dot" -> score = raw_dot(a,b) * model_scale_correction; if scoring_mode=="cosine" -> score = (raw_dot(a,b) / (l2(a)*l2(b))). If normalized_flag==true, skip divide and use raw_dot. model_scale_correction is a lightweight per-model scalar currently estimated from evaluation runs and recorded in model metadata.
4) Add an API parameter to the rerank endpoint: score_metric ("dot"|"cosine"|"auto") and a compatibility flag legacy_norm_preserve (boolean). "auto" preserves previous inference behavior for existing clients by reading their account scoring_mode and legacy flags.
5) Provide an SDK shim that sets score_metric when calling rerank/embeddings to match historical client behavior; SDK will default to account scoring_mode, but allow explicit override.
6) Migration helpers: a) provide a server-side batch job that can compute and attach l2_norm fields for existing indices without full re-materialization (compute from stored vectors), b) provide a reindex tool that can optionally normalize and rewrite vectors for customers who want to move to cosine-first scoring.

Rollout and safety:
- Feature gated behind runtime flag; default for new accounts is conservative (auto + compute l2_norm at creation).
- Canary rollout: 5% traffic for 48 hours with detailed telemetry comparing historical and new scoring outputs on a sampled prompt set and internal eval prompts.
- If score deltas exceed configured thresholds (per-customer), automatically toggle legacy_norm_preserve for that account until they opt-in to the new behavior.

Telemetry and alerting:
- Add a metric: rerank_score_delta_pct (distribution of relative change between old and new scoring for same queries).
- Create a dashboard showing top-affected accounts, percentile deltas, and request rate vs. delta.
- Add an incident runbook: threshold breach -> notify Solutions + CS -> contact customer with recommended migration path.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for transform chain on normalized/un-normalized inputs across float16/float32 quantized paths.
- Integration tests exercising SDK shim and server-side account metadata paths.
- Performance benchmarks to ensure score computation adds <5% p95 latency for rerank path when l2_norm is read from index cache.
- Backcompat test harness: replay historical recorded requests (sanitized) against both old and new scoring logic and assert numeric equality when legacy flags are set.

Open design decisions (to be resolved in design review):
- Whether to store normalized vector optionally (cost vs latency tradeoff). Storing normalized vector removes a divide at score time but increases storage by vector size.
- How to compute model_scale_correction deterministically for third-party open models; currently propose to derive via small eval dataset per model.

Success criteria:
- No customer-visible score regressions after canary for >95% of accounts, and automated legacy toggle keeps affected accounts stable.
- Latency increase on reranker path <5% p95.
- Migration job can compute l2_norm for existing indices at at least 50k vectors/min on staging instance type.

Work items (rough):
- runtime: implement scoring adapter, add account metadata layer, model_scale metadata support (ENG-31022).
- sdk: add shim and defaults (ENG-31110).
- infra: index batch job for l2_norm computation and reindex tool (ENG-31200).
- qa: create backcompat harness and benchmark suite (ENG-31234).
comments: 2026-03-10 Priya Desai: Initial ticket created after customer call where two enterprise accounts reported reordering when upgrading SDKs. Attached request traces and anonymized vectors sample.

2026-03-11 Liam Chen: Ran offline repro: when client normalizes on write but server uses raw dot, scores were ~30% higher for top candidates vs server-normalized-cosine. Added test cases to reproduce.

2026-03-12 Product (Aisha Morales): PM feedback - we need to ensure documentation and console flags are available so customers can self-service migration; add Confluence migration guide link to attachments.
2026-03-13 Design (Marco Lee): UX suggestion - expose per-route scoring preview in Console rerank debug panel so customers can compare dot vs cosine for their dataset before switching.

2026-03-14 Liam Chen: Implemented runtime adapter prototype in local branch. Bench numbers: additional cost for reading l2_norm from index cache is 1.8% p95, storing normalized vector reduced cost to 0.6% but increased mem by ~6% in index. Pushing PR for initial review: GH-PR-8241.
